sections.title: Boundary Types
paras: There is an additional boundary type in this game, which is the restricted terrain boundary (a mountainous terrain depiction). Restricted terrain occurs as follows: (i) between area 31 (Capo di Orlando) and area 32 (Randazzo), (ii) between area 33 (Adrano) and area 34 (Sant’ Agata di Militello, and (iii) **all** boundaries adjoining area 27 (Mount Etna). It takes a unit **all MP** to enter and armor class units may not enter. EXCEPTION—units belonging to the side that currently controls area 27 may use the roads to enter and exit (avoiding the restricted terrain boundary movement cost), including armor-class units, but they may only enter if area 27 is currently uncontested.
_Figure: the restricted terrain boundary (mountainous terrain depiction) around area 27 on the map._

sections.title: Appropriate Entry Areas
paras: These are areas that units may arrive in on their turn of entry. Definitions of terms and special rules used for entry are provided below.

sections.title: Allied Landing Boxes
paras: A landing box is an area with an arrow that points to a specific named and numbered coastal area on the land mass of Sicily. These coastal areas are “invasion-capable” for scenario purposes. The Allied landing boxes are labeled A1 to A4, B1 to B6 and D1 to D13.

sections.title: Allied Beachheads
paras: The beachhead markers are placed in the landing boxes for the beaches the Allies have chosen to invade, where they remain for the rest of the game unless captured. When the Allied player places a beachhead marker in a landing box, that area becomes a “beachhead”. After the first game turn of any scenario is complete, if the coastal area the beachhead is attached to is ever Axis-controlled and uncontested, the beachhead marker is destroyed and placed on the Eliminated Large Units Track. Then that landing box may no longer be used as a beachhead.

sections.title: Port Boxes
paras: A port box is an area with an arrow that points to a specific port symbol located in a specific coastal area on the land mass of Sicily, which represents a Sicilian port. There are four port boxes labeled P1 to P4: box P1 (Syracuse), box P2 (Catania), box P3 (Palermo) and box P4 (Messina). Either side may use Engineers to damage or repair the three Allied-accessible ports (P1 through P3, see 14.5). Port boxes may be used as appropriate entry areas if the ports are both undamaged and friendly-controlled for the appropriate army shown in each port box.

sections.title: Unit Arrival
paras: Arriving units are placed during the Reinforcement Phase (4.1c). Arriving airborne units are placed in the Airborne Assault holding box (regardless of stacking) and will conduct an Airborne Assault during the Combat Phase (14.27a). All other arriving units are placed on appropriate landing boxes and/or undamaged port boxes, not more than two units per box.

**a)** **Advance to Coastal Area**—Arriving units are advanced from the landing box or port box to the directly connected coastal area during the next Movement Phase (14.26). Unless an arriving unit is placed in reserve (per 14.24c), no arriving unit may remain in a landing box or port box for any reason (it must try to advance to the directly connected coastal area at some point during the Operational Movement Phase).

**b)** **Remain at Sea**—Allied units not placed in reserve that are unable to advance to a coastal area (because this would cause overstacking) must be removed from the landing box or port box and placed in the At Sea holding box instead. Units in the At Sea holding box must wait to try to enter at an eligible beachhead or port box again on the next turn (according to the Unit Arrival procedure).

**c)** **Arriving in Reserve**—Allied units may be placed in reserve rather than advancing from an eligible undamaged port box to the connected port area. These units may strat-move within the limits of 14.82, but only if the port area is uncontested at the beginning of the Strategic Movement Phase. Otherwise reserve units must land in the connected port area during the Breakthrough Phase; if still unable to do so they are placed in the At Sea holding box (see above).

sections.title: Specific Entry Areas
paras: **a)** **Axis Entry Area**—Axis units may only arrive by being placed in the port box of Messina (P4), and only if Messina is friendly-controlled.
**b)** **American Entry Area**—American units may arrive on any of the four US beachheads that remain in play, or in the port box of Palermo (P3), if undamaged and friendly-controlled.

**c)** **British Entry Area**—British units may arrive on any of the five British beachheads that remain in play, or in the port boxes of Catania (P2) and/or Syracuse (P1), if undamaged and friendly-controlled.

sections.title: Movement on Turn of Entry
paras: Once units are placed in landing and/or port boxes, they must advance to the directly connected coastal areas during each player’s next available Movement Phase (except for reserves (14.24c)).

• _Beachhead_—Allied units that arrive at a beachhead expend their entire movement allowance to advance to the directly connected coastal areas. They may not be placed in reserve. If the area is newly contested as a result of this advancement, the attacking units are conducting a Beach Assault (14.27b). Otherwise, if the area is already contested, the landing units may participate in Combat normally.
• _Allowed Ports_—Units that arrive from an allowed port box are advanced to the connected port area and then may conduct a normal movement phase with no movement penalty.

sections.title: Allied Assaults
paras: There are three forms of assault that can arise in combat situations: River Assault (5.35e), Allied Airborne Assault and Allied Beach Assault. If one or more of these assault conditions applies in a newly contested area (only), a River Assault marker is placed to indicate that the assault penalty applies in combat. Note that the River Assault penalties on the Ground Fire Combat Table apply to all three forms of assault, but if more than one type of assault occurs in an area, (such as a River Assault and an Allied Airborne Assault), resolve the combat as follows:
| Given this combination of assaults... | Resolve as... |
| Airborne Assault and any others | Airborne Assault |
| Beach Assault and River Assault | Beach Assault |
| Any one type of assault | That type |

**a)** **Allied Airborne Assault**—Arriving Allied airborne units (two units each of the American 82nd Airborne and the British 1st Airbourne) are placed in the Airborne Assault holding box (not an eligible beachhead) during the appropriate Reinforcement Phase (4.1c). The two Airborne assets do not use Airborne Assault (they function as battle assets).

• _Air Drop_—At the start of the Combat Phase (before any combats have taken place), all units in the Airborne Assault holding box must be placed into land areas as follows: each one **can only** be placed in an area that is adjacent to at least two other areas already containing units from the airborne unit’s army. If this is not possible without causing overstacking, the unit is eliminated. Note that the selected area may contain friendly and/or enemy units.

• _Assault_—After placement, **all** enemy-occupied areas with a just placed airborne unit in them resolve combat before combat in any other area takes place. The airborne unit must be the point unit. In addition, treat the combat as a River Assault (see Ground Fire Combat Table) regardless of whether other friendly units are involved (and how they moved into the area). Airborne units surviving this combat phase operate normally. An airborne assault **may not** be aborted; every hit inflicted by the defenders must be taken.
**b)** **Allied Beach Assault**—This affects Allied (non-airborne) units that arrive in a newly-contested coastal area via a landing box or flanking invasion (17.22).

• _Landing_—Arriving Allied units are advanced from a beachhead to a directly connected coastal area during the turn of entry (14.24 & 14.26). If the area is newly contested, place a River Assault marker in the newly-contested area. Note that all units in the beachhead box (one or two) are advanced and will participate in the following combat.

• _Assault_—Combat is mandatory. Treat the combat as a River Assault (see Ground Fire Combat Table), however, if the attack is aborted, the attackers must use Sea Retreat (14.28). Note that in this case the beachhead is captured by the Axis and is worth a VP to the Axis player.

sections.title: Allied Sea Retreat
paras: During the Combat Phase, Allied units in a coastal area connected to a beachhead (only) may retreat to sea if there is no other retreat option (6.6) available. Such units are placed in the At Sea holding box. Any units in the At Sea holding box must try to enter at an eligible beachhead or port on the next turn (according to the Unit Arrival procedure).

sections.title: Axis Evacuation
paras: During the Movement Phase, Axis units moving normally, may move to Messina (area 29) and then expend one available MP to evacuate to the Italian mainland—represented by the toe of Italy on the map. Once evacuated, no unit may return to play. An Axis unit may use an eligible strat-move to perform an evacuation, strat-moving normally to Messina and then to the toe of Italy.

sections.title: Allied Army Boundaries & Zones
paras: The army boundaries on the map indicate the areas that each Allied Higher Echelon (army) is responsible for.
• The areas within each army’s boundaries are collectively called that army’s **zone**.

• For reference purposes, the four zones defined by the boundaries drawn on the map are defined as zones A, B, C, and D. The zones comprising each army’s boundaries are defined in the scenario selected (see 22.0).
• IMPORTANT—Allied assets may only be played to support units of their own nationality (even those outside the normally allowed zone) or to affect areas in their army’s allowable zones (see 22.0).

• Units of the US 7th Army and of the British 8th Army can be released via Special Action (14.61) or by event (17.23) from their original zones. The status for each unit is maintained in the US and British Restricted Formation Status boxes on the map.
• Axis units are not affected by Allied army boundaries.

sections.title: Axis Army Boundaries
paras: None.

sections.title: Allied Movement Restrictions
paras: Crossing a restricted army boundary is not allowed unless the formation in question has been released from boundary restrictions (14.61 & 17.23). Even then, crossing certain boundaries (and operating in those zones) is prohibited: American units may never move into zone B, except for the area of Messina, which is in both zones B and C. Likewise, British units may never enter zone D.

sections.title: Movement Into an Area with Untried Units
paras: Either side entering an area that is solely occupied by Italian Untried unit(s) does not incur the +1 MP penalty (5.32) for congestion. Allied units must stop when entering.

sections.title: Allied Retreat Restrictions
paras: An Allied unit cannot retreat across a restricted army boundary or into an area in a prohibited zone unless it is the only path of retreat available per 6.6. If a valid retreat path exists in the unit’s current army operating zone, including the use of sea retreat (14.28), it must be used before any retreat path crossing a restricted or prohibited boundary can be used. In the restricted army boundary case, this unit’s division (only) is considered released (14.61) without the expenditure of a Special Action. If the unit is prohibited from operating in the area, it must leave the prohibited area at the first opportunity and it may not enter an enemy-occupied or enemy-controlled area as it attempts to do so.

sections.title: Additional Engineering Functions (4.3)
paras: An engineer may be used either to damage (Axis) or repair (Allies) one port. EXCEPTION: Messina may not be damaged. Ports may receive up to two levels of damage (damage markers specific to each port show either **1** or **2**). A port may only be damaged or repaired one level per Admin Phase. The port must be friendly-controlled and in supply to perform this function, and for the Allies, occupied by a British (Catania or Syracuse) or American (Palermo) unit.

sections.title: Allied Engineering Considerations
paras: In cases where a river boundary coincides with an army boundary, the bridging functions may be done by an engineer from either Higher Echelon from its appropriate adjacent area, provided the area in that engineer’s zone meets all the other requirements (4.31 & 4.32).

sections.title: Axis Engineering Considerations
paras: Axis engineer assets may be used in any zone, and may construct field works (4.33) for any Axis unit.

sections.title: Additional Special Action Uses & Staff Functions
Additional Allied Special Action Use: Release a Division
paras: The Allies may expend a special action in the Admin Phase to release any one division from having to adhere to army boundaries. Released divisions should have their matching Restricted Formation counter flipped from its “restricted” side to its “released” side in the Restricted Formation Status boxes. 7th Army units that have been released are still restricted from operating in zone B and 8th Army units are still restricted from operating in zone D. For each British division released, one of the three independent brigades (1st Canadian, 4th Armour or 231st Infantry) may also be released as part of the same special action usage. Using single-use Special Actions in this manner will only release units of the matching Army.

sections.title: Additional Command Staff Functions
paras: None for this game.

sections.title: Restriction on the Axis Staff Asset
paras: The Axis staff asset may not replace units on the board. Instead, when it uses its replacement ability (8.31), it may move any one Italian infantry (only) asset from the Eliminated Box immediately to the Available Box.

sections.title: Exclusion of Special Action Use: Reroute Reinforcement
paras: The Reroute Reinforcement (8.27) special action use is not used in this game.

sections.title: Reserve Marker Eligibility
paras: For all players, units are only eligible to receive a reserve marker if they are supplied, in good order, and in an uncontested area.

sections.title: Axis Reserve Marker Eligibility
paras: The Reserve markers of the Italian 6th army may be placed on any eligible Axis units, regardless of nationality and ignoring army boundaries.
_Figure: the Italian “6th Army Reserve” marker._

sections.title: Allied Reserve Marker Eligibility
paras: Reserve marker placement is restricted by nationality for the Allies. 7th army markers may only be placed on green blocks, and 8th army markers may only be placed on blue blocks, even if these units are outside their army boundary.
_Figure: the British “8th Army Reserve” and US “7th Army Reserve” markers._

sections.title: Axis Strat-move Limits
paras: The Axis may only strat-move one unit per game turn. This unit may originate in any zone and may cross army boundaries.

sections.title: Allied Strat-move Limits
paras: The Allies may strat-move one American and/or one British unit each turn. Strat-moves may only cross scenario army boundaries when the unit in question has been released from boundary restrictions.

sections.title: Axis Supply Sources
paras: Axis areas, units, and assets all trace supply to Messina, which must be friendly-controlled. Supply traces may cross army boundaries without penalty.

sections.title: Allied Supply Sources
paras: Allied areas, units, and assets of both armies trace to a beachhead of their own nationality or any friendly-controlled and undamaged port.

sections.title: Unit Rules Specific to this Game
Motorized Units
paras: _Figure: the Livorno division unit._

The Livorno division (two units) is motorized. These units have six movement points if they do not start in or enter a contested area, otherwise they move as infantry and are always treated as infantry units in combat.

sections.title: Divisional Integrity
paras: If two units of the same division are both actively participating in the same combat, they receive an extra die in combat (whether attacking or defending). This extra die is given the least effective success number between the two units at the time the dice are rolled.

sections.title: Italian Untried Units
paras: _Figure: an Italian Coastal Garrison unit (setup code S*)._

When setting up for any of the scenarios in the Playbook, the Italian Coastal / Garrison units (marked with a setup code of S*) are placed face down and randomly mixed together, then placed on the map face-down according to specific instructions in each scenario. These units are untried units and remain face-down and unknown to both players until the first time they are in combat. Note that regular Italian units (not marked with the setup code of S*) are defined as Tried units for the purposes of Fading Italian Morale (17.21).

**a)** _Movement Restrictions_—Only **one** untried unit may do something other than hold position in each Operational Movement Phase: it may move, build field works or be placed into reserve. If it moves, it moves with full movement allowance (3 MP). It may not move into an area containing enemy unit(s) unless reinforcing a battle via Special Action.
**b)** _Combat Restrictions_—Untried units:
• Are not revealed until in battle, after point units have been declared and all assets of both sides have been committed.
• Must make a Morale Check to see if the unit becomes disordered (this effect worsens as Italian morale fades) before any attacking artillery fires.

• Green troop quality untried units may never receive any positive modifiers to their success number for ground fire. The one veteran untried unit, when discovered, is elegible for all applicable modifiers..
**c)** _OOS Morale Checks_—Untried units are instantly eliminated if OOS morale checks are required of them in a Supply Phase.

**d)** _Becoming Tried Units_—If these units survive the round of combat that revealed them, they become Italian tried units and then suffer the less stringent effects for tried units as listed on the Fading Italian Morale Table.

sections.title: Asset Rules Specific to this Game
Axis Asset General Rules
paras: Axis assets may be played in any zone and support both Axis nationalities.

sections.title: Italian Battle Assets
paras: While they may support any Axis nationality, no more than one Italian Battle Asset may be committed to any battle (attacking or defending).

sections.title: Other Axis Assets
paras: All German assets and the Italian artillery assets have no special restrictions.

sections.title: Allied Asset General Rules
paras: Allied assets that are army specific may only assist units of their own army (7th or 8th). Strategic assets may be assigned to support either army.

sections.title: Naval Support Assets
paras: _Figure: the Naval Support asset._
The Allies start with four naval support assets. These can be used as normal artillery assets, except that they can only be used in coastal areas.

• _Shock and Awe_—For each combat in a coastal area, one naval support asset can be used to remove the defending field works, instead of firing as artillery. This happens as the first act of each battle, before the second naval support asset fires as artillery, if two were committed.

• _Reduction of Support_—During the Reinforcement Phase, if there is at least one naval support asset in the Used Box, move one to the Eliminated Box. This represents the fleet’s gradual withdrawal from harm’s way.

sections.title: US Rangers
paras: _Figure: the 1st Ranger asset._

Ranger assets (each marked with the special Ranger asset depiction) may, at the Allied player’s option, automatically remove the enemy’s Field Works marker instead of rolling their combat die. This removal is done before calculating the success number for other units and assets involved in the same battle. The attack must not have been aborted and the Ranger must have survived defensive fire to perform this option.

sections.title: British Commandos
paras: The one British Commando asset (the 3rd CDO—marked with the special Ranger asset depiction) has the same combat option listed for the American Rangers in 16.22 above. Additionally, once per game only, this asset may be used as an event to make a flanking invasion (see 17.22) during any Admin phase.

sections.title: Air Support Assets (Both Sides)
paras: _Figure: the Air Support asset._
Air support assets are flexible and can be used in the following ways regardless of the supply status of the area to which they are committed.

sections.title: Dogfighting
paras: Use during the Admin Phase (cancel an Interdiction Mission), the Combat Phase (cancel a Ground Support Mission) or the Supply Phase (cancel an Air Supply Mission).

• _How to Use_—If either player commits an air support asset to any of the missions below, the other player may cancel the stated mission by playing one of his own air support assets, in addition to the allowed artillery and battle assets.
• _Results_—Both assets are placed in the Used Box and neither player may commit more assets to replace the cancelled mission.

sections.title: Ground Support Mission
paras: Use during the Combat Phase.
• _How to Use_—Play during the Assign Assets steps of the Combat Round (6.22 & 6.23). Only one air support asset per side may be committed to each battle.

• _Dogfighting Sequence_—The first player to commit an air support asset to a battle (attacker commits assets first) allows the other player to play an air support asset for Dogfighting, if desired, as his allowed air commitment to the battle. If the defender is the first to commit an air support asset to the battle (6.23), the attacker may play an air support asset for Dogfighting – out of sequence (an exception to the sequence in the Combat Round) – as his allowed air commitment to the battle.

• _Results_—If a Ground Support mission (played by either or both players) is not cancelled by Dogfighting, an air support asset committed to a battle is used in one of the following two ways. Afterwards, it is placed in the Used Box, even if the attack was aborted.

• As an artillery asset, it fires when friendly artillery fire is resolved, but it does not count against the limit of useable artillery assets for the combat. The choice to use the Ground Support mission as an artillery asset must be made before friendly artillery fire is rolled.

• As a battle support asset, it gives direct support to one unit present, owning player’s choice, providing a **+2** modifier to that unit’s Success Number. A step-loss may **not** be assigned to the Ground Support mission.

sections.title: Interdiction Mission
paras: Use during the Admin Phase.
• _How to Use_—Place the air support asset on a land area during the Admin Phase.

• _Results_—The opposing player must pay one additional movement point to enter **and** to leave the affected area. The opposing player may **not** strat-move into or out of the interdicted area. The asset remains in the affected area until the Supply Phase of the same Player-turn, when it is moved to the Used Box.

sections.title: Air Supply Mission
paras: Use during the Supply Phase.
• _How to Use_—Place the air support asset on one unsupplied area at any time during the Supply Phase.

• _Results_—The area, the friendly units, and any assets with them are now supplied as follows: (1) the unsupplied marker is not removed and the effects of 9.34a (no assets assigned) and 9.34d (no events, Special Actions, Staff Functions or engineering functions allowed) are still in force **but** (2) the effects of 9.34b (morale check) and 9.34c (no disorder adjustment) are **not** in effect during this Supply Phase. The asset is then placed in the Used Box.

sections.title: Airfields and Their Effect on Air Support Assets
paras: The Allies have three conditional air support assets (marked with a **C** as their turn of arrival). These are placed, one each, in the three holding boxes of the Captured Airfields Track.

Each time that the Allies capture one of the three Sicilian airfields for the first time, one of these Allied conditional assets is immediately placed in the Selection Cup. Additionally, the Axis Player must fill the now empty holding box with the next Axis air support asset that arrives into the Available Box from the Selection Cup (no effect on air support assets already in the Available or Used Boxes). Players move eliminated units, assets and events to their respective Eliminated Boxes and place any large eliminated units on the Large Eliminated Units Track (19.2).

sections.title: Ports and Their Effect on Allied Asset Draws
paras: In addition to their effect on Fading Italian Morale (see 17.21), capturing intact ports has a positive effect on Allied asset/event draws. For each undamaged Sicilian port the Allies both control and currently occupy with at least one unit, add one to the asset/event chits that the Allies are allowed to draw during each Admin Phase. _For Example, if it is turn 7 and the Allies control two undamaged ports, they would draw 13/7 instead of 11/5 for that turn._

sections.title: Axis Events
paras: Axis events are not restricted by zone or nationality.

sections.title: Patton Soldier Slap
paras: _Figure: the “Patton Soldier Slap” event (turn 8, strategic)._

_Patton’s staff had to divert some of their energies into damage control after Patton slapped two soldiers in field hospitals. Historically this happened in early August, but it could have occurred earlier._
• This event is played during an Admin Phase, and stays in effect through the remainder of the game.

• The effect of this event is that it will now take the expenditure of **two** single-use US Special Action events to allow their use either to perform a Special Action or for the alternate event use (4.21). This restriction does not apply to the reusable Special Action or British single-use Special Actions.

sections.title: Axis Tactical Extract
paras: _Figure: the “Axis Tactical Extract” event (turn 5, strategic)._

When played, all German (not Italian) units are allowed to move directly from a contested area into an adjacent enemy-controlled and/or another adjacent contested area for the entire ensuing movement phase. The areas moved between may not be newly contested, nor may the area moved to be further away from Messina than the area exited (in terms of areas distant). The moving German units are marked as Recovering at the end of this move (they cannot attack, but will be in good order for the Allied player turn).

sections.title: Allied Events
paras: Unless an Allied event indicates that it is specific to one army, it may be used without regard to nationality or army boundary.

sections.title: Fading Italian Morale
paras: _Figure: the “Fading Italian Morale” event (conditional, C)._

These events have a C instead of a turn number for their turn of arrival, indicating that they are conditional. There are three of them and they are initially placed in the Captured Ports and Key VP Areas box on the Allied side of the map. Each time a triggering action occurs, one Fading Italian Morale event is added to the Allied selection cup until all three have been added.
**a)** _Triggering Actions_—The triggering actions are:
• _Functional Port Captured_—Add an available event to the Allied selection cup the instant that each Sicilian port is both Allied-controlled and undamaged for the first time.

• _Area of Battlefield Importance Captured_—Add an available event to the Allied selection cup the instant the Allies first capture each of the five areas of battlefield importance (yellow stars) for the first time.
• _Catania (Area 26)_—This area can trigger both of the above actions either simultaneously or independently.
**b)** _Level of Italian Morale_—There are three levels of worsening Italian Morale.

• _Level 1, 2 & 3_—When the first, second and third (last) Fading Italian Morale event is drawn from the Allied selection cup and is played for its listed event, each one is placed on the Fading Italian Morale Track on the Axis side of the map in the corresponding Level 1, 2 or 3 box.
For each level of Italian Morale, there are negative impacts defined below. All of these defined effects are briefly summarized on a player aid.
**c)** _Impact on Axis Asset/Event Draws_—These effects occur during the Admin Phase when the Allied Player plays a Fading Italian Morale event for its listed event.
• _Level 1_—When the **first** event is played, the Axis Player immediately moves **one** Italian asset in the Available Box to the Eliminated Box.

• _Level 2_—When the **second** event is played, first the Axis Player and then the Allied Player immediately **each** select one Italian asset in the Available Box and moves it to the Eliminated Box. Up to a total of two Italian assets could be eliminated.

• _Level 3_—When the **third** event is played, first the Axis Player and then the Allied Player immediately **each** select **two** Italian assets in the Available Box and moves them to the Eliminated Box. Up to a total of four Italian assets could be eliminated.
• In all of the above cases, The Staff Asset may not be selected to be eliminated

**d)** _Impact on Italian Untried Units_—These effects occur during the Reveal Units step (6.24) of the Combat Phase or when an OOS morale check is required. The level in effect is based on how many Fading Italian Morale events have been drawn in prior Admin Phases and placed onto the Faded Italian Morale Track.
• _At Start_—Only the Italian Untried Unit morale check is in effect (15.3).
• _Level 1_—All Italian Untried Units in the combat are automatically disordered.

• _Level 2 & 3_—All Italian Untried Units in the combat are automatically disordered and then each must make a morale check. Any unit that fails this morale check suffers a step loss and may possibly surrender (17.21f).

**e)** _Impact on Italian Tried Units_—These effects occur during the Reveal Units step (6.24) of the Combat Phase whether or not the units are already revealed. The level in effect is based on how many Fading Italian Morale events have been drawn in prior Admin Phases and placed onto the Faded Italian Morale Track.
• _Level 1_—All good order and recovering Italian Tried Units in the combat must make a morale check. Any unit that fails this morale check is disordered.
• _Level 2_—All Italian Tried Units in the combat are automatically disordered.

• _Level 3_—Any already disordered Italian Tried units in the combat each must make a morale check. Any unit that fails this morale check suffers a step loss and may possibly surrender (17.21f). All good order and recovering Italian Tried Units in the combat are automatically disordered.

**f)** _Surrender_—If an Italian unit fails a required morale check in the Reveal Units step (6.24) of Combat, use the morale check roll to determine whether the unit surrenders: veteran disordered units that roll a **10** or green disordered units that roll an **8-10** surrender. The surrendering unit is eliminated. Any attacking armor receives an exploitation opportunity if the area is no longer contested, either from step-loss or surrender.

sections.title: Flanking Invasion
paras: _Figure: the 30 RCT (-) and 3rd CDO battle assets._

There are three 1-pip battle assets (two US assets, each representing different battalions of the 30th RCT, and one British asset, the 3rd CDO) that have a dual purpose as Flanking Invasion events. When used as an event, one of these assets may be placed during the Admin Phase onto an enemy-controlled, uncontested coastal area within two areas of any unit from the same army that is also in a coastal area (only one per Admin Phase).

• If the area is enemy-occupied, a round of combat is immediately fought during the Admin Phase of the landing with asset constraints (see below). The flanking invasion asset is considered to be making a beach assault (14.27b) for purposes of success number modification.

• The Allied player can only commit air support and/or naval support assets (not artillery or battle assets) during the landing and for as long as the flanking invasion remains in the area. The Axis player has no unusual restrictions.

• If the flanking invasion survives this round of combat, or if the area was unoccupied, the asset will remain in the area as follows until it is eliminated in combat or relieved: (i) it may not initiate combat (defend only), (ii) although it does not control the area, enemy units cannot retreat into the area, (iii) it does not have to trace supply, and (iv) it does not block enemy supply.

• The asset is relieved the instant an Allied unit enters the area by being placed in the Used Box. Note that 3rd CDO asset may only be used once per game as a flanking invasion event while a 30th RCT asset may be used for its flanking invasion capability each time it is in the Available Box during an Admin Phase.

sections.title: US 7th Army Release
paras: _Figure: the “US 7th Army Release” event (turn 3)._

All six US divisions are released from having to adhere to Army boundaries (except that they still cannot enter zone B). This allows them to now enter zone A or zone D, depending on the invasion scenario chosen. Released divisions should have their matching Restricted Formation counter flipped from its “restricted” side to its “released” side in the Restricted Formation Status boxes.

sections.title: Infantry Replacement
paras: _Figure: the “Br Inf Non-Elite Repl” (turn 2) and “US Inf Non-Elite Repl” (turn 8) events._

This event may be used to provide one **non-elite step** to increase the current strength of any supplied, **reduced** infantry-class unit of the indicated nationality, even in a contested area. Eliminated units may not be returned by use of a replacement event.

sections.title: Armor Replacement
paras: Used exactly as the infantry replacement above, except that it affects armor-class units.

sections.title: Special Action
paras: _Figure: the “Special Action” event (turn 4)._
These events are single-use Special Actions (8.1) which may be used for any purpose outlined in the Special Action rules (8.2).

sections.title: Asset Delayed
paras: _Figure: the “Asset Delayed” event (turn 8)._

This represents early battlefield confusion for the Allies and the later effect of Allied fighter-bombers on the Germans. When these are drawn they are immediately placed in the Eliminated Box, with no positive effect for the drawing player. Asset delayed events drawn **do** count as one of your allowed draws from the Selection Cup.

sections.title: Optional Rules
paras: _These rules add more “chrome” to the game. Use and mix these rules as desired when agreed upon by both players._

sections.title: Airborne Units
paras: The American 82nd and the British 1st Airborne Divisions were specially trained and equipped to operate behind enemy lines with minimal supply. The four units of these two divisions (only) ignore the usual **–1** unsupplied morale check modifier (6.7).

sections.title: Advanced Artillery Modifiers
paras: _Artillery is generally less effective against defenders and more effective against infantry-class targets than armor-class targets._
Add the following Success Number Modifiers for artillery fire:
**–1** Target is the Defender
**+1** Target’s point unit is infantry-class and not in Field Works.

sections.title: Overrunning Artillery
paras: If the Defender had an artillery asset in a combat and the area was vacated of defending units, there is a chance the defending artillery asset will be overrun and destroyed. If the Defender retreated, but at least one step survived, the artillery asset is destroyed on a die-roll with a Success Number of **1**. If the defending units and battle assets were destroyed, the Success Number becomes **2**. Add one to the Success Number for each unabsorbed hit from the combat. Roll one die for each involved defending artillery asset.

sections.title: Maintaining Field Works
paras: Instead of removing Field Works from a contested area automatically during a Supply Phase, have the controlling player make a morale check for one unit of his choice within the area during friendly Supply Phases (only). The Field Works marker is only removed by absorbing a hit or by failure of this morale check.

sections.title: Determining Victory
paras: Players earn Victory Points (VP’s) by securing Objective Areas and by eliminating beachheads and certain enemy units.

sections.title: Objective Areas Victory Points
paras: An Objective Area must be both friendly-controlled AND be able to trace a valid supply path (9.31) for a player to be awarded its VP(s) during the Victory Check Phase. Objective Area symbols show who is awarded the VP’s for control of them as follows:
• **Areas Near Messina**—These areas have German crosses marking them. Only the Allied player is awarded VP’s for control of these areas and only if currently occupied by at least one Allied unit.
• **Coastal Areas of Importance far from Messina**—These areas have white stars marking them. Only the German player is awarded VP’s for control of these areas.

• **Areas of Battlefield Importance**—These areas have yellow stars marking them. Both players are awarded VP’s for control of these areas. The Allies are only awarded VP’s for these areas if they are currently occupied by at least one Allied unit.

sections.title: Eliminated Large Unit Adjustment
paras: Each eliminated unit which has three or more steps on the unit label is worth one VP to the opposing player. Such units should be placed on the Eliminated Large Units Track as they are eliminated. Smaller units and assets do not have a VP value. Captured Allied beachhead markers are also worth a point each to the Axis player and are also placed on the Eliminated Large Units Track.

sections.title: Calculating Victory Points
paras: _Figure: the VPs marker._

During the Victory Check Phase of each turn, both players sum the VP’s they are awarded for Objective Areas they control per 19.1 above, then add the number of eliminated enemy large units (which may include captured Allied beachhead markers), and then compare those totals. The difference between those totals is the current VP level, with the player having the higher total being the advantaged player. Use the VP marker provided, which has a German side and an Allied side, placing it on the General Information Track to reflect the advantaged player and the current VP level.

sections.title: Sudden Death Victory
paras: Beginning with turn 4, the Turn Record Chart shows what is needed in terms of net Victory Points (yours minus his) to end the game in a Sudden Death Victory during the Victory Check Phase for each of these turns. If neither player has achieved the net Victory Points needed to end the game, play proceeds to the next Game Turn.

sections.title: Overview
paras: Use this short scenario to introduce yourself to the rules. The goal is simple — seize and control the special VP areas marked right on the small map.

sections.title: Scenario Length
paras: Play Game Turns 1-4 only.

sections.title: Area of Play
paras: • Use the Sunrise Bridge map sheet included in the game. Only the areas on this map sheet are in play. All land areas start Axis-controlled.
• Use the Scenario Forces sheet included in the game. It contains the complete listing of forces (units, assets and events) at start and subsequent turns.
• Use the Scenario Information sheet included in the game. It contains the necessary holding boxes, time track and asset draws for the scenario.
• Place the Scenario Forces sheet and Scenario Information sheet next to the Sunrise Bridge map sheet for both players to use. The main map is not needed to play.

sections.title: Deployment at Start
paras: Reference the Scenario Forces sheet for the units deployed at start on the map (Axis) or arriving during the Reinforcement Phase (Allied)
• _Axis Deployment of Regular Units_—First the Axis player deploys German and Italian units with a starting area number in those locations at full strength.

• _Axis Deployment of Coastal Garrisons_—Then the Axis player deploys the ten Italian Coastal Garrisons (units with an S*) as follows: all these units are shuffled face-down and placed, one per area, on the Sunrise Bridge map sheet in areas 1-7, 13, 14 and 26.
• _Axis Fortification_—Finally the Axis player places a field works marker on each coastal area that (a) is invasion-capable and (b) has at least one Axis unit in the area.

• _Allied Landing_—The Allied player places the five British beachhead markers in the following landing boxes: B1 through B5. Once the deployment of beachhead markers is done, the Allied player places his units onto the beachheads and the Airborne Assault holding box (14.24), which completes the Reinforcement Phase of Game Turn 1.

sections.title: Reinforcements
paras: Reference the Scenario Forces sheet for the arriving units, assets and events for both sides. All units arrive at full strength.

sections.title: Special Scenario Rules
paras: All Series and Exclusive rules are in effect unless modified by this scenario.

• British forces are constrained to land and operate in Zone B (14.3 & 14.4) unless specifically released by use of special action (14.61) to enter into areas in Zone A (areas 7, 10, 11, 17, 16 and 25).

• Neither player may voluntarily exit units off the map, with the exception of Allied Sea Retreat (14.28); the Scenario Information sheet contains the At Sea holding box for Sea Retreat. Otherwise, units forced off the map for any reason are considered eliminated.
• The requirements and restrictions for Italian Untried Units are in effect (15.3) including the avoidance of a movement congestion penalty (14.42).
• Fading Italian Morale (17.21) as triggered by the conditional assets (16.4) and events (16.5) is not used.

• The Axis supply source rule (14.91) is modified: a unit is in supply if it can trace a supply path into one of the following friendly-controlled areas: areas 16, 17, 25 or 26. The Allied supply source rule (14.92) is unchanged.

sections.title: Victory
paras: Victory is determined at the end of Turn 4 by awarding VP for control of the following areas:
• 1 VP for control of Areas 6, 7 and 10 through 17
• 2 VP for control of Areas 5 and 16
• 3 VP for control of Area 25
• 4 VP for control of Catania (area 26)

These values are included on the Sunrise Bridge map sheet. Elimination of large units does not apply in this scenario. After the VP for area control is calculated for both players, the difference between the two values is calculated. The player with positive net VP is the winner, otherwise the game is a draw.

sections.title: Historical Outcome
paras: The British 8th Army faced unexpected difficulty in pushing up the Sicilian coast towards Mount Etna, a naturally impressive and forbidding defensive feature used to great advantage by the Italian 6th Army.

sections.title: Overview
paras: This is the standard scenario, representing the period from the landings on July 10, 1943 through July 19, 1943. Playing this game to completion should take experienced players about three hours. The Allied player must press the attack as strongly as possible, including the achievement of one or more breakouts and/or encirclements of the Axis positions.

sections.title: Scenario Length
paras: Play 5 Game Turns unless a Sudden Death Victory is achieved.

sections.title: Area of Play
paras: The entire map is used. All land areas of Sicily are Axis-controlled.

sections.title: Deployment at Start
paras: • _Units, Assets and Events at Start_—All scheduled units will be deployed (Axis) or arrive (Allied) at full strength. All scheduled assets and events are placed in the Available Box but note the Turn 1 Sequence Exception (22.27). See the At Start reference cards for both players.
• _Axis Deployment of Regular Units_—First the Axis player deploys German and Italian units with a starting area number in those locations at full strength.

• _Axis Deployment of Italian Coastal Garrisons_—Then the Axis player deploys Italian Coastal Garrisons (units with an S*) as follows: all these units are shuffled face-down and placed, one per area, anywhere in Sicily that the Axis Player desires, including areas that already contain a tried unit, but not areas that already contain two tried units.
• _Axis Fortification_—Finally the Axis player places a field works marker on each coastal area that (a) is invasion-capable and (b) has at least one Axis unit in the area.

• _Allied Invasion Planning_—Now the Allied player examines the Axis setup and may freely choose one of the following two invasion choices: (a) the **Historical Landing Plan** (22.25) or (b) the **Alternate Landing Plan** (22.26).

• _Allied Landing_—Once the deployment of beachhead markers is done (according to the selected landing plan), the Allied player places his invasion units (with an **Inv**) onto the beachheads and the Airborne Assault holding box (14.24), which completes the setup.

sections.title: The Historical Landing Plan
paras: • _British Deployment_—The Allied player chooses any five consecutive landing boxes in **zone B** and places the 5 British beachhead markers in them. British units may only operate in zone B unless released from boundary restrictions (allowing them to also operate in zones A & C).

• _American Deployment_—The Allied player places the 4 American beachhead markers in the landing boxes for **zone A**. American units may only operate in zones A & C unless released from boundary restrictions (allowing them to also operate in zone D).

sections.title: The Alternate Landing Plan
paras: • _British Deployment_—The Allied player chooses any five consecutive landing boxes in and across **zones A and/or B** and places the 5 British beachhead markers in them. British units may only operate in zones A & B unless released from boundary restrictions (allowing them to also operate in zone C).

• _American Deployment_—The Allied player chooses any four consecutive landing boxes in **zone D** and places the 4 American beachhead markers in them. American units may only operate in zones C&D unless released from boundary restrictions (allowing them to also operate in zone A).

sections.title: Special Scenario Rules
paras: • _Rules_—All Series and Exclusive Rules are in effect thus all areas, zones and boundaries are in effect.
• _Turn 1 Sequence Exception_—The scenario begins with the Allied Operational Movement Phase skipping the Allied Admin Phase. All other player turns proceed according to the sequence of play.
• _Reinforcements_—All scheduled units, assets and events listed on the Reinforcement reference cards for both players are available and arrive at full strength.

sections.title: Victory
paras: If a Sudden Death Victory was not achieved, then the VPs are calculated per 19.3 and the final tally is compared to the following table:
• **Axis 4 or more VPs** = Axis win
• **Axis 3 or less VPs** = Allied win

sections.title: Historical Outcome
paras: After the initial landings, the American landing zones faced ferocious counterattacks by mobile German units, while the British landing zones gained a better footing at first. Over the following nine days, the balance of difficulty switched sides, with the British 8th Army facing a much greater resistance before them, whereas the American 7th Army, ordered to change its direction, advanced rapidly westward.

sections.title: Overview
paras: This is the long game, representing the period from the landings on July 10, 1943 through July 31, 1943. Playing this game to completion should take experienced players four to five hours. This is the scenario that gives the players the maximum scope for exploring various landing plans and defensive deployments.

sections.title: Scenario Length
paras: Play all 9 Game Turns unless a Sudden Death Victory is achieved.

sections.title: Area of Play
paras: The entire map is used. All land areas of Sicily are Axis-controlled.

sections.title: Deployment at Start
paras: This is identical to the Tournament Scenario.

sections.title: The Historical Landing Plan
paras: This is identical to the Tournament Scenario.

sections.title: The Alternate Landing Plan
paras: This is identical to the Tournament Scenario.

sections.title: Special Scenario Rules
paras: • _Rules_—All Series and Exclusive Rules are in effect thus all areas, zones and boundaries are in effect.
• _Turn 1 Sequence Exception_—The scenario begins with the Allied Operational Movement Phase skipping the Allied Admin Phase. All other player turns proceed according to the sequence of play.
• _Reinforcements_—All scheduled units, assets and events listed on the Reinforcement reference cards for both players are available and arrive at full strength.
• **Special Historical Scenario Option**: Players desiring to play a strictly historical version of the campaign use the Tournament Scenario deployment rules (22.24) with the following alterations.

• Italian Coastal Garrisons (29 in total) are still shuffled face down as described in 22.24, but may only be placed into the following areas: (a) one unit in each of the 23 invasion-capable coastal areas and (b) one unit in coastal areas 26, 28, 29, 30, 48 and 49.
• The Allied player uses the Historical Landing Plan as described in 22.25 with one additional restriction: the British beachheads must be boxes B1 through B5.

sections.title: Victory
paras: If a Sudden Death Victory was not achieved, then the VP’s are calculated per 19.3 and the final tally is compared to the following table:
• **4+ VPs** = Operational Victory for the side with the VP’s
• **1-3 VPs** = Marginal Victory for the side with the VP’s
• **0 VPs** = Draw

sections.title: Historical Outcome
paras: By the end of July, it was clear to the combatants that Operation Husky, the largest amphibious invasion ever undertaken, had proven that the Allied partners could effectively conduct a massive combined operation under extreme circumstances (beach landings into difficult mountainous terrain). The pathway via the “underbelly” looked very bright for the foreseeable future, despite missed opportunities and some brilliant defensive maneuvering.

sections.title: Designer’s Notes
paras: This game took a bit longer than I intended to bring to your table, but I wanted it to be right. I feel confident that **_FAB volume II_** is indeed ready for action and I feel that it even surpasses the gaming experience we enjoyed in volume I.

The main problem was scale, as this campaign involved far fewer divisions that the battle of the bulge, but the amount of territory was similar. The terrain in Sicily is very rugged, and the battle eventually results in a very narrow front as Messina is approached.

I eventually settled on a scale of one battalion per pip (about half the scale of volume I) and made each division two units and an asset, and also added a divisional integrity rule to effectively encourage players to keep their divisions together.
The next challenge was to effectively divide the island into areas. You will notice more areas that meet at a point in Sicily, this is intentional and an aspect of the difficult terrain.

After a very long time fine-tuning everything to my satisfaction, I took the game for a test drive, and the long effort paid off handsomely in a game that was both fun and gave the correct feel of the campaign.
I have had enormous fun playtesting and fine tuning the game you now hold in your hands. It is my sincere hope it brings you the same fun and excitement for many years to come.
I apologize for the delay in getting volume II into your hands, but I hope you’ll agree that it was worth the wait.
Enjoy the game!
—_Rick Young_

sections.title: Axis Player
paras: The Axis player needs to hold on, as long as he can, to the airfields, ports, and battlefield objectives. Always be on the lookout for opportunities where the Allies have left a lone block or a critical area exposed to possible counterattack, but be careful you are not placing your counterattacking units in a noose.

As Italian Morale fades, you will have no choice but to shorten your line and back up towards Messina, with an eye on getting your Italians out of the line before they afford the Allies a few easy VPs.

Special Actions are usually best spent buying replacement steps for your German units. As your Italian non-garrison units get reduced to 1-step, pull them off the line and get them off the island. They are not worth anything to you alive, but they are worth a VP each to the Allies if they can hunt them down.

sections.title: Allied Player
paras: You have a tough job ahead. You must put pressure all along the line and try to stretch the Axis front to the breaking point.
The Luftwaffe will be quite annoying in cancelling your own airpower until you start securing the airfields.
Make use of your flanking invasions, they will interdict movement and cut retreat paths, forcing the Axis to deal with them rather than strengthening his front.
You have a lot of assets that can negate enemy field works (rangers, commandos, naval support, and engineers), use one whenever possible as enemy field works will otherwise slow you down too much.

sections.title: Beachhead Selection & Setup
paras: **Overview—** We start with beachhead selection because this is fundamental to understanding the challenge of this design. Around the coast of the island of Sicily there are three ranges of landing boxes pointing to land areas, representing the places Allied planners considered for invasion sites. The historic sites (A1 through A4 and B1 through B6) have specific codenames associated with each of the historic landing sites. The sites labeled D1 through D13 do not have codenames but that entire stretch was considered during Allied planning. In this design, the Axis player does not know whether the Allied player will select the historic plan or some alternate plan. His challenge is to face this unknown. The Allied player will have enough intelligence to see generally where the Axis player has deployed and can ponder his options. The attractions for a historic approach or an alternate approach are different. Which will you pick?

**A—** The players have chosen to play the Campaign Scenario, which allows the Allied player to pick either the Historical Landing Plan or the Alternate Landing Plan. The Allied player chooses the latter, which permits him to land 7th Army (US) forces in any four contiguous landing boxes in Zone D. This represents the selected alternative invasion site for the US forces. Each landing box points to one specific land area on the island of Sicily. During the Reinforcement Phase, the player will place any arriving US units into designated landing boxes (or beachheads). During the Movement Phase, units in beachheads advance (consuming their entire movement point allowance) to the directly connected land areas.

**B—** There are four port boxes on the map, two subject to British use – Syracuse [P1] and Catania [P2], one subject to US use – Palermo [P3] and one subject to German use – Messina [P4]. They cannot be used as beachheads and so cannot be marked by a beachhead marker. Note that a port is an area that can be entered from either a designated landing box (beachhead) or a port box. Once the port of Palermo [57] is Allied-controlled and uncontested, and the Palermo port box [P3] is fully operational (no damage), then the Allied player can place arriving US reinforcements into the Palermo port box [P3]. During the Movement Phase, units in port boxes not only move directly to the port area but may continue moving.

**C—** During scenario preparation, after the Allied player selects the landing plan (per scenario instructions), then he places beachhead markers into specific landing boxes in the appropriate zones. There are thirteen landing boxes in Zone D for the Allied player to choose from. In this case, he decides to place markers in landing boxes D2 through D5, giving him direct access to Palermo [57] and adjacent access to Marsala [65]. Once placed, the beachhead markers cannot be moved, although they can be captured (and permanently eliminated) by the Axis player.

**D—** Once a beachhead marker is placed into a landing box, the beachhead is formally created. It is now ready to support unit arrival. During the Reinforcement Phase, arriving units are placed into available and appropriate beachheads. During the immediately ensuing Movement Phase, units in beachheads are directly advanced from the landing box to the directly connected land area. This process of arrival and advancement to a land area is identical for port boxes, once the proper conditions for control are in place.

**E—** As part of his defensive planning, the Axis player has to decide how to place the many weak Italian Coastal Garrison units (with entry notation S*). A handful of them will put up enough resistance to cause some steps of damage to the Allied invader, but neither player knows which will actually do so. Because of this, the Axis player places all of them face down, randomly shuffles them, and then places them (per the scenario directions) into desired areas across the island. If he places them in an invasion-capable area (one that is pointed to by a landing box), he can beef them up with a field works marker at start. Does he place them at the water, in poor terrain, with a field works marker likely to be nullified by Allied Ranger or Naval Support assets or does he place them inland in better terrain, while yielding to his opponent an easy landing?

**F—** As part of setup, the Axis player also places specific Axis units in predetermined areas (per scenario directions). These units have the area number with yellow highlight as the entry notation. Unlike the coastal garrisons (which represent a practically unknown force), the primary, organized units of the Italian 6th Army were disposed in locations that Allied reconnaissance had mostly determined prior to the invasion. The flexibility of the coastal garrison deployment, therefore, restores to the Axis player more of a chance to induce some doubt in the Allied player’s decision as to where to land.

_Figure: Western Sicily from Marsala [65] to Termini Imerese, with US beachhead markers in landing boxes D2 through D5 (A Landing Box, C Beachhead Marker, D Beachhead at D4), the Palermo port box [P3] “Allied Control Required (7th Army only)” (B Port Box), face-down coastal garrisons with field works markers in coastal areas (E), and an Italian unit set up in its predetermined area beside a garrison (F)._

sections.title: Draw of Assets & Events
paras: **Overview—** Units, assets and events arrive during the Reinforcement Phase, which happens only at the start of the Game Turn. Both players receive units, assets and events (with a turn of arrival notation, such as **3** for entry on Turn 3). Aside from units already in place at the start of the game, Axis units arrive via the Messina port box [P4]. Allied units must always arrive via beachheads or controlled, undamaged port boxes. Assets and events are placed directly into each player’s Selection Cup, which by play convention are opaque cups (coffee cups, paper cups and so on). Although players know what resources are scheduled to arrive (according to plan), they may only immediately receive some of what they expected (requisitions denied or resources lost in transit). At the beginning of the Admin Phase, both players draw a certain number of counters from their own Selection Cups as specified for that turn. For example, on Turn 3, during the Admin Phase of the Allied player turn, the Allied player may draw 11 counters, while the Axis player may draw only 10 counters. Later during the Admin Phase of the Axis player turn, both players may draw 5 counters. Only after the counters are drawn will the players see what assets and events they have actually received.

**A—** Both players have a Resources section on the map particular to their needs. Certain parts of the sequence of play are listed in the various boxes with a numbered sequence (so the players can perform the necessary steps in order without referring to the player aids). First, the Allied player reviews what he must do in the Reinforcement Phase (using Turn 3 in this example). He sees that he has the Reusable Special Action in the Available Box (step 1 in the Available Box), which allows him to immediately retrieve a used asset from the Used Box. Unless the Allied player saves the Naval Support asset, it must be eliminated (step 3 in the Used Box). He retrieves the Naval Support asset.

**B—** The listed steps (2 and 3) in the Used Box now no longer apply: the Reusable Action was already in the Available Box and no Naval Support assets are in the Used Box (with one subject to elimination). Next, the Allied player places all the remaining used assets into the Selection Cup (step 4 in the Used Box). Back in the Reinforcement Box, step 5 directs the Allied player to place all the assets and events arriving for the turn (in this case, Turn 3) into the Selection Cup as well.

_Figure: The Allied Resources section of the map (Available Box, Used Box, Eliminated Box) with their numbered Reinforcement Phase steps; the Naval Support asset is moved from the Used Box to the Available Box (A) and the remaining used assets are put into the Selection Cup (B)._
_Figure: The Allied Resources section after the draw: the counters drawn from the Selection Cup in the Available Box (C) and the additional US 7th Army Release event (+1)._

**C—** After both players have completed what they must do in the Reinforcement Phase, it is now the Admin Phase, starting with the Allied player. He looks at the Available Box and sees he is directed to draw counters from the Selection Cup. According to the calendar on the Turn Track, he may draw 11 counters from the Selection Cup, placing them in the Available Box. In addition, since he controls and occupies the undamaged port of Syracuse [5], he may draw one additional asset, the US 7th Army Release event (giving good fortune for the Allied player). He drew no further Naval Support assets, so it turns out that saving the Naval Support asset was a good choice.

**Asset and Event Play—** After drawing the scheduled number of assets and events, the Allied player can now play certain assets and events as desired. The Action Matrix and the Event Summary Table are organized by phase to remind players of the choices they can make with their resources. The Asset Capability Matrix provides even more detail about particular effects of asset play, especially decomposing their use in the Combat Phase. Aside from the ever-valuable Reusable Special Action, two excellent choices for the Allied player would be (i) the possible play of the 3rd CDO asset as a Flanking Invasion in Catania [26] or Lentini [14] to maintain maximum disruption at a crucial defensive point for the Axis player and (ii) the definite play of the US 7th Army Release event, giving immediate breathing room to the scope of Allied advance.

sections.title: Air Interdiction & Dogfighting
paras: **Overview—** Air Support assets can be played in the Admin Phase (Interdiction mission), Combat Phase (Ground Support mission) or Supply Phase (Air Supply mission) or by the other player (Dogfighting mission) to immediately cancel the attempted mission in each of those phases.

**A—** During the Axis Player Turn, the Axis player intends to moves his major units on the western end of the island eastwards to respond to the Allied invasion. After the Axis portion of the Admin Phase, the Allied player (during his portion of the Admin Phase) commits Air Support assets to the Interdiction mission to stall the Axis response to Allied progress. He takes two Air Support assets from the Available Box and places one each in Bolognetta [56] and Salemi [59]. Each Allied Air Support asset used for Interdiction will cause any Axis units to pay +1 MP to enter and +1 MP to leave the interdicted area.

**B—** Although it is no longer the Axis portion of the Admin Phase, either player may commit Air Support assets to the Dogfighting mission, which enables that player to cancel one enemy Air Support mission per asset played. The Axis player realizes that his amount of Air Support is much less than for the Allied player, however, he is not willing to have all his units stalled due to Interdiction. He immediately commits his one available Air Support asset to the Dogfighting mission in Salemi [59], which cancels the Allied Air Interdiction mission. This restores freedom of movement to the units in Salemi [59]. Since he does not cancel the Interdiction mission in Bolognetta [56], that mission succeeds and persists until the Axis Supply Phase, when the asset is removed to the Allied Used Box.

**C—** In the Axis Movement Phase, the Axis player is faced with a less than ideal situation. Assume in these examples that either moving unit is not in the way of the other unit (to avoid explaining potential congestion penalties). The Italian unit in Palermo [57] cannot get past Bolognetta [56] since it has only 3 MP to expend: 1 MP along the road plus 1 MP for Interdiction and it cannot leave the area because it must spend at least 2 more MP to leave. At best, it can make its way to Corleone [54] via Rocca Busambra [55]. The Italian unit in Alcamo [58] faces the same problem and cannot go farther than either Bolognetta [56] or Corleone [54]. The Axis player decided to protect his more mobile German armor units in Salemi [59]. These units can take the road south to Castelvetrano [60] and thence along the coast to reach either Canicatti [40] or Palma di Montechiaro [41], moving significantly towards the action on the eastern end of the island. Alternatively, they could reach Caltanissetta [45] via legal road movement using Corleone [54], Prizzi [50], Collesano [48] and Castelbuono [46] (since primary roads connecting adjacent areas do not have to be literally connected to each other inside an area).

_Figure: Western Sicily around Palermo [57]: Allied Air Support assets placed for Interdiction in Salemi [59] and Bolognetta [56] (A), the Axis Air Support asset sent Dogfighting into Salemi [59], cancelling that Interdiction (B), and the Italian units in Palermo [57] and Alcamo [58] moving with their MP costs (1 MP, 2 MP, 3 MP, STOP at Bolognetta), while the German armor in Salemi [59] heads south and east._

sections.title: Port Damage & Repair
paras: **A—** During the Reinforcement Phase of Game Turn 3, the Allied player has a US unit arriving, one of the two US 9th Infantry blocks. The battle for Palermo [57] is concluded, with a badly battered 1st Infantry block remaining in the area as a garrison. While the Allied player now controls Palermo [57] because an Allied unit was the last sole occupant of the area, he cannot yet use the Palermo port box [P3] because the port itself (as represented by the port box) is damaged. The consequence for the Allied player is that the sorely needed reinforcement can only be advanced from the beachhead [D2] to Palermo [57] as its sole action during the Movement Phase.

**B—** During the Allied portion of the Admin Phase, the Allied player decides to use an available Engineer asset to repair the port box one level (from Damage 2 to Damage 1). A necessary condition for the play of this asset is that the port area (Palermo [57] itself) must be friendly-controlled, in supply and (for the Allied player) occupied by a US unit. Since Palermo [57] is friendly-controlled, in supply and occupied by the US 1st Infantry, all three conditions are in place for the Allied player to play the Engineer asset to make the repair of the Palermo port box [P3].

**C—** The play of the Engineer asset causes the Damage 2 marker to be flipped to its Damage 1 side. The port box [P3] itself continues to remain unusable, and will remain that way unless and until the Allied player plays yet another available Engineer asset during an Admin Phase that will remove the Damage 1 marker. The Axis player may not, during the ensuing Axis portion of the Admin Phase, play an available Engineer asset to cause the damage to go back up to Damage 2. This is because Palermo [57] is not friendly-controlled and in supply (from the Axis perspective). Were the Axis player able to battle back to Palermo [57], solely occupy it and thereby control it, he could then (in an ensuing Admin Phase) damage the port box [P3] once again.

_Figure: Palermo [57] and the Palermo port box [P3] “Allied Control Required (7th Army only)”: the arriving US unit is placed in the US beachhead in landing box D2 (A), the 540th Engineer asset is played on the port box (B), and the Damage 2 marker on the port box is flipped to Damage 1 (C)._

sections.title: Army Boundaries
paras: **Overview—** The Allied army is divided into two higher echelons, the 8th Army (British) and the 7th Army (US), which must operate together within some challenging boundary restrictions. The areas within an army’s boundary are collectively referred to by a zone ID. The zones are not strictly fixed, however, since a key to the game focuses on which landing plan the Allied player chooses (based on the Axis disposition). For example, when the Allied player uses the Historical Landing Plan, the British forces must land and operate in Zone B and the US forces must land and operate in Zones A and C (see the map). Zone D represents another operating area, which the forces may move into when formally released (via special actions or events). If the Allied player uses the Alternate Landing Plan, British forces can land and operate in both Zones B & A, whereas the US forces must land in Zone D and may operate in Zones D and C. When released, British forces may additionally operate in Zone C, whereas US forces may additionally operate in Zone A. In all cases, no US force may ever operate in Zone B and no British force may ever operate in Zone D. The scenarios outline the specific conditions depending on the selected landing plan. For clarity, all the components of this example assume the Historical Landing Plan boundary definitions.

_Figure: Central Sicily with the Zone A / Zone C boundary: the British 5th Infantry in Mount Etna [27] (A), the British 51st Infantry in Catania [26] (B), the US 2nd Armor in Leonforte [24] (C), the US 1st Infantry in Enna [38] (D), the 1st Canadian in Mazzarino [39] (E) and the US 45th Infantry in Ramacca [16] (F), each with its divisional release marker and its possible moves marked “Yes”, “NO” or “Never”._

**A—** The British 5th Infantry in Mount Etna [27] is currently operating in Zone B. The divisional release marker in the 8th Army Boundary Restrictions box indicates that the unit is restricted (for clarity, the appropriate divisional release markers are placed on the map next to the designated units). In this state, the unit may not yet move into Adrano [33] in Zone C, nor may it yet move to Regalbuto [25] in Zone A. When released, both moves will become legal.

**B—** The British 51st Infantry in Catania [26] is currently operating in Zone B. The divisional release marker indicates that the unit is released. In this state, the unit may move to Regalbuto [25] in Zone A and may continue on to Adrano [33] in Zone C.

**C—** The US 2nd Infantry in Leonforte [24] is currently operating in Zone A. The divisional release marker indicates that the unit is restricted. In this state, the unit may already move into Nicosia [35] in Zone C, but it may not yet move to Caltanissetta [45] in Zone D. When released, the latter move will become legal.

**D—** The US 1st Infantry in Enna [38] is currently operating in Zone A. The divisional release marker indicates that the unit is released. In this state, the unit may already move to Gangi [37] in Zone C and it may now move to Castelbuono [46] in Zone D.

**E—** The 1st Canadian Infantry (8th Army) in Mazzarino [39] is currently operating in Zone A. The divisional release marker indicates that the unit is released. In this state, it may operate throughout Zones A, B and C, but it may never voluntarily enter Zone D (the 8th Army is prohibited from operating in that zone).

**F—** The US 45th Infantry in Ramacca [16] is currently operating in Zone A. The divisional release marker indicates that the unit is restricted. In this state, it may only operate in Zone A. When released, it may then additionally operate in Zones C and D, but it may never voluntarily enter Zone A (the 7th Army is prohibited from operating in that zone).

**Release—** Release from army boundary restrictions is accomplished in the following ways: (1) The 7th Army can be entirely released by the play of the 7th Army Release event, or individual 7th Army formations can be released via play of a Special Action and (2) The 8th Army can **only** be released formation by formation via play of a Special Action. Note that when you release an 8th Army division, you can simultaneously release one of the three independent Brigades (1st Canadian, 4th Armour, and 231st Infantry).

**Retreat—** While you may not voluntarily violate an army boundary restriction, it is possible that there is no other way to properly conduct a retreat. In such a case, it depends on whether the unit is forced across a “restricted” army boundary (in which case, it will become released to operate in the eligible zone) or across a “prohibited” army boundary (in which case, it must attempt to return as quickly and directly as possible to an eligible zone).

sections.title: Basic Movement
paras: **Movement and Boundaries—** There are two standard boundary types in the game: open and river. River boundaries always have bridges. When units move across the boundaries, the type of connection they use — road or field — defines the movement cost. When a primary road crosses the boundary of an area into another area — whether the boundary is open or river — that makes the connection a **road** connection. Otherwise, that connection — whether the boundary is open or river — is a **field** connection. Note that the road depictions inside an area do not have to connect with one another.

**A—** The mechanized German 15th PG unit moves south into Monti Sicani [51], costing 1 MP for the road connection. The unrevealed Italian Untried unit does not impose a penalty on moving Axis units for congestion (since it is Untried, it is unclear whether it will function and to what degree). Then it moves into Aragona [43], costing an additional 2 MP for the field connection, and on to Canicatti [40] for an additional 2 MP for the field connection for a total of 5 MP spent. It cannot enter Caltanissetta [45] to attack the US 9th Infantry unit since it needs two more MP to do it: 1 MP for the road connection and +1 MP to enter an occupied area.

**B—** The mechanized unit moves into Mussomeli [44], costing 3MP (2 MP for the field connection and +1 MP to enter an occupied area), and on to Castelbuono [46], costing an additional 1 MP only for the road connection (no congestion penalty applies due to the unrevealed Italian Untried unit). Because the congestion penalty does not apply, the mechanized unit has enough MP to enter Caltanissetta [45] to attack the US unit: 1 MP for the road connection and +1 MP to enter an occupied area.

**C—** The mechanized unit swings northward into Collesano [48], costing 1 MP for the road connection, then on to Castelbuono [46], costing an additional 1 MP only for the road connection (no congestion penalty applies due to the unrevealed Italian Untried unit). Note that primary roads connecting adjacent areas do not have to be literally connected to each other inside an area (a viable road network is assumed in these particular cases). The mechanized unit can not enter Caltanissetta [45] to attack the US unit: 1 MP for the road connection and +1 MP to enter an occupied area. With a total of 4 MP spent, this is clearly the fastest way to reach the target area.

**D—** The motorized Italian Livorno unit moves directly ahead into Mussomeli [44], costing 3 MP (2 MP for the field connection and +1 MP to enter an occupied area). It must stop for two reasons: (1) No unit may cross a blown bridge unless it started in the area with the boundary marked by the blown bridge (that is, “directly adjacent”), thus, the unit cannot enter into Caltanissetta [45]; (2) The motorized Italian Livorno division (both blocks) normally has an MP allowance of 3, but this can be increased to 6 if during the entire MP expenditure it neither leaves nor enters an enemy-occupied area; it therefore cannot seek to use this additional movement capability to enter the target area since this would negate the availability of the additional MP.

**E—** The motorized unit can move into Mussomeli [44], costing 3 MP and continue on to Castelbuono [46], costing an additional 1 MP only, leaving potentially 2 MP to spend (using its motorized capability). However, it is not permitted to enter the enemy-occupied Caltanissetta [45] when using the motorized movement bonus, and thus it must stop. It might continue eastwards down the road, or to unoccupied Enna [38] for its final 2 MP (motorized).

**F—** The motorized unit can also swing northward into Collesano [48], costing 1 MP for the road connection, then on to Castelbuono [46], costing an additional 1 MP only for the road connection (no congestion penalty applies due to the unrevealed Italian Untried unit). But it still cannot enter Caltanissetta [45] since to enter will require an additional 2 MP (1 MP for the road connection and +1 MP to enter an occupied area). It cannot reach the target area whether using its infantry mode (3 MP) or its motorized mode (6 MP).

**G—** Italian Untried units are severely restricted in terms of what they can do. Only one Untried unit can do anything other than hold position during an Operational Movement Phase. Otherwise, Untried units remain where originally placed unless (i) one of them is selected to “do something” (move, build field works or be placed into reserve) or (ii) Allied units “try” them in combat by entering the area (and they survive).

_Figure: The area around Mussomeli [44] and Caltanissetta [45]: the German 15th PG unit’s routes A, B and C and the Italian Livorno unit’s routes D, E and F with cumulative MP (1 MP, 2 MP, 3 MP, 4 MP, 5 MP, 6 MP), a Blown Bridge marker on the Platani River boundary into Caltanissetta [45], the US unit in Caltanissetta [45], and unrevealed Italian Untried units, one in Monti Sicani [51] (G)._

sections.title: Restricted Terrain Boundaries
paras: **Overview—** The area of Mount Etna [27] is bounded on all accessible sides by the restricted terrain boundary depiction. Infantry class units must expend their entire movement allowance to cross that boundary. Armor class units are strictly prohibited from crossing the boundary. The exception to these restrictions is that the side that controls the area enables friendly units to use road connections into and out of the area.

**A—** The armor class German 15th PG in Catania [26] can enter Mount Etna [27] costing 1 MP for the road connection, +1 MP to exit a contested area and +1 MP to enter an occupied area. The unit can also use road connections to pass through the area. It enters Mount Etna [27] for 3 MP, then crosses over to Adrano [33] costing 1 MP for the road connection and stops.
